content.value_statement: Memory bugs cause crashes, leaks, and security defects in systems software. This skill gives practical patterns for safer resource ownership across C, C++, and Rust.
actual_capabilities: Explains common memory bug categories and prevention strategies.
Shows RAII wrappers for files, locks, transactions, and resources in C++.
Demonstrates Rust ownership, borrowing, lifetimes, Rc, Arc, and Mutex patterns.
Presents C cleanup patterns with create and destroy functions.
Compares safe container access, bounds checking, and data race prevention techniques.
Lists debugging tools such as AddressSanitizer, Valgrind, Miri, and ThreadSanitizer.
limitations: It provides examples and guidance, not automated static analysis.
It does not verify that copied snippets compile in every project.
It does not replace language-specific security review or testing.
It focuses on memory safety, not broader application security.

use_cases.title: Harden C++ Resource Management
use_cases.description: Use RAII and smart pointer patterns to reduce leaks, double frees, and unsafe manual cleanup.

use_cases.title: Plan Rust Ownership Models
use_cases.description: Map shared state, borrowing, lifetimes, and concurrency choices before implementing Rust components.

use_cases.title: Audit C Cleanup Paths
use_cases.description: Review create and destroy flows, goto cleanup blocks, and local resource ownership contracts.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Memory Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the main memory safety risks in my C or C++ module. Focus on ownership, cleanup, and bounds checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Ownership Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between unique ownership, shared ownership, borrowing, or cleanup functions for this resource design.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor For RAII
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this C++ resource management design and suggest a RAII wrapper, move behavior, and safe destructor strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Cross-Language Safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare C, C++, and Rust approaches for this concurrency-heavy component. Recommend memory safety patterns and testing tools.

output_examples.input: I need to manage a file handle in C++ without leaks.
output: Use a RAII wrapper that owns the file handle and closes it in the destructor.
Delete copy operations, allow move operations, and keep ownership transfer explicit.
Add error handling at construction so invalid resources cannot escape.

output_examples.input: My Rust service shares counters across worker threads.
output: Use Arc for shared ownership across threads.
Use atomics for simple counters and Mutex or RwLock for compound state.
Join worker handles and handle lock errors deliberately.

output_examples.input: I am reviewing a C API that allocates several resources.
output: Define clear create and destroy functions for every owned resource.
Use one cleanup path that frees resources in reverse allocation order.
Document which function owns each pointer after every call.

best_practices: Prefer ownership models that make cleanup automatic and visible.
Use safe containers and checked access when correctness matters.
Run sanitizers and memory tools on critical code paths.
anti_patterns: Do not share mutable state without an explicit synchronization strategy.
Do not hide resource ownership behind unclear raw pointer contracts.
Do not copy examples without adapting error handling and lifecycle rules.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on C, C++, and Rust, with brief comparisons to managed languages.

faq.question: Can it find memory bugs automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and patterns, but it does not run analyzers or inspect binaries.

faq.question: Is it useful for new Rust developers?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains ownership, borrowing, lifetimes, reference counting, and thread-safe sharing.

faq.question: Does it replace AddressSanitizer or Valgrind?
faq.answer: No. It recommends these tools, but testing and runtime analysis are still required.

faq.question: Can it help modernize older C++ code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide changes from raw resource handling to RAII and smart pointers.

faq.question: What should I provide when using it?
faq.answer: Provide the language, resource type, ownership expectations, concurrency model, and failure handling requirements.
